title: Coherent modules on a locally Noetherian scheme: kernels, cokernels, sums, quasi-coherent sub- and quotient modules
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with its kernels (sectionwise) and cokernels (sheafified sectionwise quotients). (1) If $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], then $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ are coherent; if $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are coherent, so is $\mathcal F\oplus\mathcal G$. (2) If $\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module, then $\mathcal F'$ and the quotient $\mathcal F/\mathcal F'$ (the cokernel of the inclusion) are coherent.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y0 (lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian, line 2310: kernel and cokernel of a map of coherent modules are coherent, any extension of coherent sheaves is coherent; restatement of Modules, Lemma 01BY, modules-lemma-coherent-abelian) and Lemma 01Y1 (lemma-coherent-Noetherian-quasi-coherent-sub-quotient, line 2329)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum] to the underlying ringed space for kernels and cokernels. Apply its coherent-extension clause to the canonical split short exact sequence F → F ⊕ G → G to obtain binary sum closure. Mathlib ShortComplex.Splitting.ofHasBinaryBiproduct and Splitting.shortExact construct this sequence.

For a coherent F and a quasi-coherent submodule i : F′ → F, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] gives quasi-coherence and finite type of F. Pull finite local generators to the slice over an affine open U (the proved private restriction lemma for arbitrary sheaves of rings on sites with binary products and pullbacks, weak sheafification on first-level slices and sheafification on iterated slices). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] to obtain finite Γ(F,U). Local Noetherianity makes Γ(X,U) Noetherian. Evaluation preserves the monomorphism i, hence its map on sections is injective; Mathlib isNoetherian_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite and Module.Finite.of_injective show that Γ(F′,U) is finite. This uses the finite-module Noetherian instance in the Mathlib match of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc]; no sheaf ACC theorem is needed.

All affine opens cover X by Mathlib iSup_affineOpens_eq_top. The affine-cover clause of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] gives finite type of F′. Together with its assumed quasi-coherence, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] gives coherence. Apply the cokernel clause of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum] to i to prove coherence of the quotient.

split_report.summary: Split along Cohomology of Schemes Lemmas 01Y0 and 01Y1. Three steps reduce to affine opens of a locally Noetherian scheme, use the coherent iff quasi-coherent finite-type criterion and the existing quasi-coherent kernel/cokernel computations, then apply Noetherian finite-module closure to obtain finite type for kernels, cokernels, direct sums, and quasi-coherent submodules and quotients. All reusable ingredients are existing DAG nodes; no private proof lemma or new child node was introduced. The item’s recorded LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, and Mathlib grep audits correctly find no coherent-sheaf closure theorem in Mathlib.

lean.statement: theorem isCoherent_kernel_cokernel_biprod_and_submodule (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] : (∀ (F G : X.Modules), RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G → (∀ (φ : F ⟶ G), RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (kernel φ) ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (cokernel φ)) ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (F ⊞ G)) ∧ (∀ (F F' : X.Modules) (i : F' ⟶ F), RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F → Mono i → SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F' → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F' ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (cokernel i))
